provenance.paper_title: GeoForge: Non-Parametric Self-Evolving Agents for Earth-Observation Reasoning

evidence.paraphrase: A reliability-aware directed graph stores Earth-observation workflow nodes, tool-transition edges, usage statistics, sensing dependencies, and operation order for task-conditioned traversal.
Compact action lessons preserve local tool corrections and are retrieved as part of the task-conditioned inference context.

evidence.section: Full paper: Adapted Skill SOP and Evidence-Grounded Execution
evidence.paraphrase: A persistent adapted SOP records reusable procedures, data requirements, and parameter constraints and is concatenated with graph and action memories at inference.
After execution, a distiller converts the compacted grounded trajectory into reusable action lessons, a revised SOP, and workflow candidates while excluding sample-specific shortcuts.
The distiller proposes textual and structured memory edits, and a safety gate controls whether the revised SOP replaces the persistent prior.
Graph updates normalize and merge candidate workflows by tool-sequence and lexical similarity, while action experiences are inserted only after deduplication.
The workflow-graph updater prunes stored structures using their accumulated reliability after merging new candidates.

evidence.section: Full paper: Evidence-Grounded Execution and Safety-Gated Self-Evolution
evidence.paraphrase: At inference, completed tool executions and their grounded outcomes generate a safety-gated revised SOP and workflow candidates; accepted artifacts persist in the nonparametric state and are retrieved to govern operation selection and composition on later Earth-observation tasks.

adjudication_notes: Strict T3 is supported because the update follows inference-time tool execution, changes reusable SOP/workflow policy artifacts rather than only logging the episode, persists them in the external state, and injects them into future execution contexts.
